body:
When trying to append data to a table in parallel, I see all the commits eventually wait in a queue and update the metadata one after another. I know that is to guarantee an atomic swap and get a linear history of changes. But it acts as we put a table-level lock on all the updates and if we would like to read the latest data of a table, we have to wait until all the swaps of the metadata are done. It feels like to me that the updates are allowed to be taken in "parallel", but actually they are done in a "serial" manner (swap the metadata one after another).
Put feel free to correct me if I am wrong. So far, I do not have mature solutions to solve that, but some initial ones (like reduce the granularity of lock to partition level?), so I would like to raise this issue as a "discuss" one. Any comments are warmly appreciated.
title: [DISCUSS] Update metadata serially

body:
In order to avoid reading manifests to get stats in #675, we need to collect additional metadata when writing manifests. The minimum required information (num added/deleted records) can be gathered easily. The main question is how to store it.
Option 1
We can store the new metadata as we store the number of added/deleted/existing files.
Benefits:

We can always retrieve the additional information by reading manifests.

Drawbacks:

Affects what we actually store on disk.
Potentially increases the metadata size.

Option 2
We can introduce a serializable field of type Map<String, String> but don't store that on disk. Only instances of ManifestFile created via ManifestWriter will always contain all needed properties.
Benefits:

The metadata on disk doesn't change.
The metadata size stays the same.

Drawbacks

We cannot retrieve the additional information by reading manifests.
title: Collect additional metadata while writing manifets

Cannot write incompatible dataset to table with schema:

However if I set checkOrdering to false in here, https://github.com/apache/incubator-iceberg/blob/949c6a98ac80acec10568070772082c1178eb739/api/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/types/CheckCompatibility.java
Result rows should match expected:<[{"id"=1,"data"="a"}, {"id"=2,"data"="b"}, {"id"=3,"data"="c"}, {"id"=4,"data"="null"}]> but was:<[{"id"=1,"data"=""}, {"id"=2,"data"=""}, {"id"=3,"data"=""}, {"id"=4,"data"="�"}]>

Actual   :[{"id"=1,"data"=""}, {"id"=2,"data"=""}, {"id"=3,"data"=""}, {"id"=4,"data"="�"}]
this is because PartitionSpec accessors are being built out of iceberg schema. If we update the code to build the accessors from the input schema, then the re-order test case passes.
this is shown in below PR

We are trying to understand if there is any specific reason to set checkOrdering to false by default and not expose it as a parameter and build the accessors in PartitionSpec from table schema instead of input schema.
And If possible , we would like to enable checkOrdering as a configurable parameter so that it can be turned off and write jobs do not have to use the same ordering as Iceberg Table.

Apart from cleaning up deleted dataFiles while expiring snapshot, the current ExpireSnapshots [code here] tries to delete underlying files added by dangling snapshots i.e. that is not parent of anybody.
With cherrypick feature with WAP, the approach is to generate a new snapshot with dataFiles of underlying WAP snapshot, and commit it on top of latest/current snapshot. This makes the WAP snapshot dangling, and when you expire this snapshot then underlying dataFiles are deleted, and making the table un-readable. Please see the gist here https://gist.github.com/mehtaashish23/fb87c57d13de8f9f56b5a1516265bfff which try to reproduce this, on top of PR #695
[code here] : https://github.com/apache/incubator-iceberg/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/apache/iceberg/RemoveSnapshots.java#L234
title: ExpireSnapshots break on top of PR https://github.com/apache/incubator-iceberg/pull/695

I would like to propose to modify Catalog.dropTable() to add an option to decide whether to delete data files when dropping the table, like: /** * Drop a table; optionally delete data and metadata files. *

* If purge is set to true the implementation should delete all data and metadata files. * * @param identifier a table identifier * @param purge if true, delete all data and metadata files in the table * @param deleteData ignored if purge is false; If purge is true and deleteData is true, delete all data and metadata files in the table If purge is true and deleteData is false, delete all metadata files while keep all data files * @return true if the table was dropped, false if the table did not exist */ boolean dropTable(TableIdentifier identifier, boolean purge, boolean deleteData); The proposal above is trying to meet the following requirement: We are in process of implementing update and delete. A staging table is introduced and its data files are referenced by the base table's manifest. When dropping the staging table (as the last step of update or delete operation), we would like to purge the metadata of the staging table while keep its data files.
title: Add an option to decide whether to delete data files in Catalog.dropTable()

    Assert.assertEquals("Residual should be alwaysTrue", alwaysTrue(), residual);

  @Test

    Schema schema = new Schema(
      Types.NestedField.optional(50, "dateint", Types.IntegerType.get()),
      Types.NestedField.optional(51, "hour", Types.IntegerType.get())
